courses.title: Forensic Science, Criminal Law and Quality Management, MSc Forensic Science Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MSc CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Criminal laws of India
topics.summary: The new criminal codes and the forensic science provisions in them.
notes: From 1 July 2024 the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced the IPC, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) the CrPC, and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) the Evidence Act.
BNSS section 176(3): forensic experts must visit the scene for offences punishable with seven years or more and the collection must be video-recorded.
BNSS section 349 lets a magistrate order specimen signatures, handwriting, finger impressions and voice samples.
BSA section 39 makes expert opinion relevant; section 63 governs electronic records.
outcomes: Map old and new criminal law provisions relevant to forensics
Explain the forensic mandates in BNSS

topics.title: The expert in court
topics.summary: Admissibility standards, report writing and cross-examination.
notes: An expert report states the materials received, methods, results, interpretation and limitations.
Indian courts treat expert opinion as advisory; the court weighs it with other evidence.
Frye (general acceptance) and Daubert (testability, peer review, error rate, standards, acceptance) are influential foreign standards.
Cognitive bias (contextual, confirmation) is reduced by blind verification and sequential unmasking.

topics.title: Accreditation and quality assurance
topics.summary: ISO/IEC 17025, validation and proficiency testing.
notes: ISO/IEC 17025 sets requirements for testing laboratory competence; NABL accredits Indian laboratories.
Method validation establishes specificity, accuracy, precision, LOD, LOQ, linearity and robustness.
Proficiency testing and inter-laboratory comparisons check performance.
Measurement uncertainty must be estimated and reported where relevant.

topics.title: Interpreting evidence statistically
topics.summary: Probability, likelihood ratios and fallacies.
notes: Likelihood ratio LR = P(E | Hp) ÷ P(E | Hd); LR > 1 supports the prosecution proposition.
Posterior odds = LR × prior odds (Bayes' theorem in odds form).
Prosecutor's fallacy confuses P(E | Hd) with P(Hd | E).
Random match probability is the chance that an unrelated person shares the profile.
outcomes: Compute and explain a likelihood ratio

lesson.hook: A blood type found at the scene occurs in 1% of people, and the suspect has it. Is there a 99% chance he is guilty?
lesson.example:
P(E | Hp) = 1, P(E | Hd) = 0.01, so LR = 100: the evidence is 100 times more likely if the suspect is the source.
With prior odds 1:1,000, posterior odds = 100 × 1/1,000 = 1:10, far from 99%.

questions.a: Treating the probability of the evidence given innocence as the probability of innocence given the evidence.

courses.title: Instrumental Methods in Forensic Analysis, MSc Forensic Science Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MSc CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: GC, HPLC and TLC
topics.summary: Theory and forensic applications of chromatography.
notes: Resolution Rs = 2(t₂ − t₁) ÷ (w₁ + w₂); Rs ≥ 1.5 means baseline separation.
Plate number N = 16(tR ÷ w)²; more plates mean sharper peaks.
GC suits volatile compounds (accelerants, alcohol, drugs); HPLC non-volatile and thermally labile ones.
outcomes: Choose a chromatographic method for a sample

topics.title: Molecular spectroscopy
topics.summary: UV-Vis, FTIR, Raman and fluorescence in forensics.
notes: FTIR and Raman give molecular fingerprints of drugs, fibres, paints and polymers.
ATR-FTIR analyses solids with little preparation.
Fluorescence detects body fluids and some inks under alternate light sources.
outcomes: Interpret FTIR spectra of common evidence

topics.title: MS and hyphenated techniques
topics.summary: Ionisation methods, analysers and GC-MS and LC-MS/MS.
notes: Ionisation: electron impact (hard, library searchable), chemical ionisation and electrospray (soft).
Analysers: quadrupole, time-of-flight, ion trap, Orbitrap.
GC-MS is the confirmatory standard for many drugs; LC-MS/MS for trace toxicology.
outcomes: Explain how GC-MS confirms a drug

topics.title: AAS, ICP, XRF and SEM-EDX
topics.summary: Elemental analysis and electron microscopy of trace evidence.
notes: AAS and ICP-MS measure trace metals (poisons, glass, soil).
XRF is non-destructive elemental analysis.
SEM-EDX identifies gunshot residue particles (lead, barium, antimony).
outcomes: Choose an elemental technique for evidence

courses.title: Forensic Biology and Serology, MSc Forensic Science Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MSc CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Hair, fibres, pollen and diatoms
topics.summary: Microscopy and identification of biological traces.
notes: Hair comparison uses colour, medulla, cuticle scales and cortex; nuclear DNA from roots, mtDNA from shafts.
Forensic palynology uses pollen to link people and places.
Diatoms in bone marrow support ante-mortem drowning.
outcomes: Use diatom tests in drowning cases

topics.title: Body fluid identification
topics.summary: Presumptive, confirmatory and immunological tests.
notes: Blood: Kastle–Meyer, luminol (presumptive); Takayama, Teichmann, immunochromatographic Hb tests (confirmatory).
Semen: acid phosphatase, PSA, sperm microscopy; saliva: amylase.
Species origin by precipitin (ring, Ouchterlony double diffusion) tests.
outcomes: Plan a sequence of tests for a stain

resources.title: Effect of temperature and pH on salivary amylase

topics.title: Wildlife crime
topics.summary: Species identification and the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.
notes: Wildlife crime includes poaching and trade in protected species and their parts.
Species are identified by morphology, microscopy and DNA barcoding (cytochrome b, COI).
The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau coordinates enforcement in India.
outcomes: Identify species from parts using DNA barcoding
Explain the legal framework for wildlife crime

topics.title: Insects and time since death
topics.summary: Insect succession and estimating the post-mortem interval.
notes: Blowflies arrive within minutes to hours; their life cycle is egg, larva (three instars), pupa, adult.
Accumulated degree hours (ADH) relate development to temperature.
Succession of insect species estimates longer intervals.
outcomes: Estimate a minimum PMI from larval stage and temperature

courses.title: Forensic DNA Profiling, MSc Forensic Science Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MSc CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: DNA structure and variation
topics.summary: DNA structure, polymorphism and markers used in forensics.
notes: DNA is a double helix of nucleotides; A pairs with T, G with C.
STRs (2–6 bp repeats) are highly polymorphic; SNPs are single-base variants.
CODIS core set has 20 STR loci; amelogenin indicates sex.

topics.title: Extraction, quantification and amplification
topics.summary: Organic, Chelex and silica extraction; qPCR; multiplex PCR.
notes: Extraction methods: organic (phenol–chloroform), Chelex-100, silica columns and magnetic beads; differential extraction separates sperm and epithelial cells.
qPCR quantifies human DNA and detects inhibitors and degradation.
PCR cycles: denaturation (≈94–95 °C), annealing (≈50–65 °C), extension (≈72 °C); copies double each cycle.

resources.title: Real-time PCR: standard curve and efficiency

topics.title: Interpretation and statistics
topics.summary: Alleles, stutter, mixtures and match statistics.
notes: Artefacts: stutter, pull-up, drop-in, drop-out and allele imbalance.
Random match probability by the product rule with Hardy–Weinberg genotype frequencies (p² homozygote, 2pq heterozygote).
Mixtures are interpreted with probabilistic genotyping software giving likelihood ratios.
outcomes: Compute genotype frequencies and an RMP

lesson.example:
At one locus alleles 12 and 15 have frequencies 0.1 and 0.2: genotype frequency 2pq = 0.04.
Across loci, frequencies multiply (product rule), giving very small RMPs.

topics.title: Y-STR, mtDNA and kinship
topics.summary: Lineage markers, paternity and disaster victim identification.
notes: Y-STRs follow the paternal line; mtDNA follows the maternal line; neither is unique to an individual.
Paternity index compares the probability of the child's alleles with the alleged father versus a random man.
Disaster victim identification combines DNA, fingerprints and dental records.
outcomes: Choose lineage markers for a case

courses.title: Forensic Toxicology and Drug Analysis, MSc Forensic Science Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MSc CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Absorption to elimination
topics.summary: Pharmacokinetics applied to poisoning and alcohol.
notes: ADME: absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion.
Widmark formula: BAC = A ÷ (W × r) − βt (A alcohol in g, W body mass, r distribution factor, β elimination rate).
Post-mortem redistribution can raise drug concentrations in central blood.
outcomes: Estimate blood alcohol with Widmark's formula

topics.title: Screening and confirmation
topics.summary: Sample preparation, immunoassays and confirmatory analysis.
notes: Extraction: liquid–liquid, solid-phase extraction, protein precipitation.
Immunoassays screen urine for drug classes; positives are confirmed by GC-MS or LC-MS/MS.
Cut-off concentrations decide positive or negative results.
outcomes: Design a screening and confirmation scheme

topics.title: Common poisons in India
topics.summary: Pesticides, plant poisons, metals and gases.
notes: Organophosphates inhibit acetylcholinesterase (treatment: atropine and oximes).
Aluminium phosphide releases phosphine gas.
Plant poisons: oleander (cardiac glycosides), datura (anticholinergic), abrus (abrin).
outcomes: Identify common poisons by symptoms and tests
Describe the mechanism of organophosphate poisoning

topics.title: Seized drug analysis
topics.summary: Sampling, identification and new psychoactive substances.
notes: Representative sampling (e.g. hypergeometric or Bayesian plans) for large seizures.
Identification needs at least two independent techniques (SWGDRUG categories).
New psychoactive substances (synthetic cannabinoids, cathinones) need updated reference standards.
outcomes: Plan sampling of a large seizure

courses.title: Questioned Documents and Fingerprint Science, MSc Forensic Science Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MSc CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Handwriting identification
topics.summary: Characteristics, standards and conclusions.
notes: Individual characteristics: letter formation, connections, proportions, alignment, pen pressure, speed.
Collected (course of business) and requested standards should be contemporaneous and adequate.
Conclusions range from identification through probable to elimination.

topics.title: Printed documents, inks and security features
topics.summary: Printers, counterfeit currency and ink dating.
notes: Printing processes: offset, inkjet, laser, intaglio (currency).
Indian banknote features: watermark, security thread, latent image, micro-lettering, intaglio, colour-shifting ink.
Inks are compared by TLC and spectroscopy; ink dating is uncertain and contested.

topics.title: Ridge detail and development
topics.summary: Levels of detail, development chemistry and AFIS.
notes: Level 1: pattern; level 2: minutiae; level 3: pores and ridge edges.
Chemistry: ninhydrin and DFO react with amino acids; physical developer with lipids; cyanoacrylate polymerises on residues.
AFIS searches databases (NAFIS in India) and returns candidates for human comparison.

resources.title: Matching a chance print by minutiae
Fingerprint patterns: arch, loop and whorl

topics.title: Footwear, tyre and tool marks
topics.summary: Comparison of impressions and marks.
notes: Class and individual (acquired) characteristics.
Gel lifters and electrostatic lifters recover dust impressions.
Tool marks are compared by comparison microscope.

courses.title: Forensic Ballistics and Physics, MSc Forensic Science Semester 3
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MSc CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: Firearms and ammunition
topics.summary: Classification, mechanisms and cartridge components.
notes: Cartridge: case, primer, propellant, projectile.
Rifling: number, direction and twist of lands and grooves are class characteristics.
Marks on cartridge cases: firing pin, breech face, ejector and extractor marks.

topics.title: Internal, external and terminal ballistics
topics.summary: Projectile motion, wound ballistics and range of fire.
notes: Kinetic energy KE = ½mv² largely determines wounding potential.
External ballistics: trajectory, drag and ricochet.
Range of fire from soot, stippling and pellet spread (shotguns).

topics.title: GSR analysis
topics.summary: Formation, collection and analysis of GSR.
notes: GSR contains lead, barium and antimony particles from the primer.
Collection by stub lifts from hands within hours of firing.
SEM-EDX identifies characteristic particles by morphology and composition.

topics.title: Glass, paint and soil
topics.summary: Physical and chemical comparison of trace evidence.
notes: Glass: refractive index (GRIM), density, elemental composition (LA-ICP-MS).
Paint layer sequences are compared by microscopy and FTIR.
Soil: colour (Munsell), particle size, minerals.
outcomes: Compare glass by RI and density

resources.title: Refractive index of glass by the Becke line

courses.title: Digital Forensics, MSc Forensic Science Semester 3
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MSc CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: Standards for digital evidence
topics.summary: ACPO principles, ISO/IEC 27037 and legal admissibility.
notes: ACPO principles: no action should change data; competent persons; audit trail; overall responsibility.
ISO/IEC 27037 guides identification, collection, acquisition and preservation.
BSA section 63 requires a certificate for electronic records.

topics.title: Acquisition and file system analysis
topics.summary: Imaging, hashing and analysis of NTFS and FAT.
notes: Write blockers prevent changes; images in E01 or raw (dd) formats.
NTFS stores file records in the MFT; deleted entries may persist.
Timeline analysis uses MAC(B) timestamps.

topics.title: Mobile devices and cloud data
topics.summary: Extraction methods, encryption and cloud evidence.
notes: Full-disk and file-based encryption limit physical extraction.
App data (SQLite databases) holds messages, locations and media.
Cloud evidence is obtained through legal process and account access with authorisation.
outcomes: Choose extraction methods for a phone

topics.title: Volatile and network evidence
topics.summary: RAM analysis and network investigation.
notes: Memory images reveal running processes, network connections, keys and malware (Volatility framework).
Logs (firewall, proxy, server) and NetFlow reconstruct activity.
Attribution must account for VPNs, Tor and spoofing.

courses.title: Forensic Medicine, Anthropology and Odontology, MSc Forensic Science Semester 3
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MSc CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: Death and post-mortem interval
topics.summary: Modes of death and estimation of time since death.
notes: Algor mortis (Henssge nomogram), livor mortis, rigor mortis, vitreous potassium.
Decomposition is accelerated by heat and slowed by cold or burial.
Autopsy determines cause, manner and mechanism of death.
outcomes: Distinguish cause, manner and mechanism of death

topics.title: Wound analysis
topics.summary: Blunt, sharp and firearm injuries and ante-mortem vs post-mortem wounds.
notes: Vital reaction (inflammation, bleeding) indicates ante-mortem injury.
Wound age is estimated from healing stages.
Pattern injuries can reflect the weapon.

topics.title: The biological profile
topics.summary: Estimating sex, age, stature and ancestry from skeletal remains.
notes: Sex: pelvis is most reliable (sub-pubic angle, greater sciatic notch), then skull.
Age: epiphyseal fusion, pubic symphysis, auricular surface, cranial sutures.
Stature from long bones with population-specific regression equations.
outcomes: Build a biological profile from bones

topics.title: Dental identification and bite marks
topics.summary: Dental charting, age estimation and bite mark analysis.
notes: Comparison of ante-mortem and post-mortem dental records (Interpol DVI forms).
Dental age from eruption and development stages (e.g. Demirjian method).
Bite mark analysis has high error rates and is now treated with great caution.
outcomes: Explain limits of bite mark evidence
